paper_metadata.title: Evolution and formation mechanism of the interfacial microstructure on diffusion bonded joints of single crystal Ni-based superalloys to Ti3AlC2 ceramic with Ni interlayer

evidence.quote: Single crystal Ni-based superalloys DD3 and nanolaminated ternary ceramics Ti3AlC2 were the critical high-temperature structural materials
The inter-diffusion between the Ni interlayer and the DD3 sub - strate was not intense. Only a diffusion layer with a thickness of ~3 μ m was formed.

evidence.quote: the bonding process was performed in the vacuum furnace ((1.3–2.0) × 10^3 Pa).
Thus, constant pressure of 30 MPa was applied to the assembly during the bonding process. At the 900 ◦C/60 min/30 MPa, a good bonding interface was obtained.
The inter-diffusion between the Ni interlayer and the DD3 sub - strate was not intense. Only a diffusion layer with a thickness of ~3 μ m was formed.

evidence.quote: A small amount of Al2O3 impurity phase can also be observed at the grain boundary of the original ceramic. It was formed in the preparation of raw ceramic materials and remained after the diffusion bonding process.

attributes.size: width 3 μm (DZ I); width >30 μm (DZ II)

evidence.quote: a diffusion zone with a width of 3 μm between DD3 and Ni interlayer was obviously observed due to the interdiffusion of elements, labeled as diffusion zone I (DZ I).
In contrast, a quite complex diffusion zone with a width of more than 30 μm was formed at the Ti3AlC2 interface, labeled as diffusion zone II (DZ II).

conditions.test_method: universal mechanical testing machine, loading rate 0.5 mm/min

evidence.quote: A strong DD3/Ti3AlC2 joint with the average shear strength of 86.4 MPa was obtained by vacuum diffusion bonding using the Ni interlayer at 900 ◦C for 60 min.

According to the shear test result, the shear strength of the diffusion bonding joint with the Ni interlayer was 86.4 MPa, increasing by 124%, compared to the direct diffusion bonding joint with the sheat strength of 38.6 MPa.
So, Al and Ti mainly existed in the DZ I region in the form of solid solution, indicating that the inter-diffusion between the Ni interlayer and the DD3 substrate was not intense.

Due to more defects in the grain boundary of the ceramic [40], the diffusion energy required of Ni along the grain boundary of the Ti3AlC2 substrate is relatively lower. Therefore, the grain boundary in the Ti3AlC2 substrate is the preferential diffusion channel of Ni during the bonding process.

It could be speculated that, as the diffusion bonding went on, the Ti3AlC2 ceramic will continue to lose stability and decomposed, releasing the Al atoms and Ti atoms, which will combine with Ni atoms to form Ni3Al and AlNi2Ti phase.
